title: A* Search on a 4-Connected 2D Obstacle Grid with Manhattan Heuristic
description: Generate a binary obstacle grid with the supplied dimensions. Define 4-connected neighbors and the Manhattan distance heuristic, and run astar between the supplied start and goal.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `numpy` and `random` and define `make_grid` with the supplied defaults. It fills an `(h, w)` array of zeros and marks cells as `1` (obstacle) with probability `obstacle_prob`.
Define `grid_neighbors(grid, cell)` to yield in-bounds 4-connected neighbors where `grid[ny, nx] == 0`. Define `grid_cost` as unit cost and `manhattan(cell, goal)` as `abs(y - gy) + abs(x - gx)`.

Notice how `grid_neighbors` allows only up, down, left, and right steps of unit cost. This matches `manhattan(cell, goal)`: the exact minimum number of 4-connected steps needed when no obstacles block the way.

steps.question: For the grid on lines 30-31, what is the Manhattan distance from the supplied start to goal without obstacles? Why is the actual `Path length` (`39`) equal to `info_grid['cost']` (`39.0`)?
steps.answer: The obstacle-free Manhattan distance is `abs(y - gy) + abs(x - gx) = 39`. Every step has unit cost, so a path of `39` steps has total cost `39.0`.

steps.description: Build the grid with the supplied dimensions, clear `grid[start] = 0` and `grid[goal] = 0`, and run `astar` with `h_manhattan`. Print `Path length: 39` and `Info: {'expanded': 192, 'pushed': 237, ..., 'cost': 39.0, 'closed_size': 192}`.
